key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though point defects create deep gap states, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic losses.
engineering_relevance: This makes t-Se a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where maintaining performance despite defects is critical.
method: Large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Comparison of nonradiative multiphonon emission and radiative capture across charge states and doping conditions
evidence_signal: The study reports multiple deep defect levels, but large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 E_G per recombination event strongly suppress recombination across the defect dataset.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on computed defect populations and idealized conditions, so device-level losses may still involve extrinsic defects, interfaces, or microstructural effects not captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
